Me and My School History

Letters to our future selves, the trips that made us laugh, and the people who shaped our years at school.

Sara Cardoso, Pilar Reyes, Sadisley Echeverría and Ema Iglesias. Senior year project.

Letters to the future

Written in our final year, sent five and ten years ahead.

Pilar

To herself, five years from now

Dear Future Me,

I am writing this letter during my last year of high school, and I can hardly believe that this stage is almost over. In five years’ time you will be twenty-three, and I hope you will be proud of the person you have become.

I am starting university next year, so by 2031 I will have been studying for about four years. I am also going to travel as much as I can: I hope I will have visited at least three new countries by then, with a camera in my bag and a notebook full of stories. At this very moment I am saving a little money every month, and I will keep doing it until I have enough for my first big trip.

I imagine you living in a small, bright apartment full of plants. I hope you will still be in touch with Sara, Ema and Sadis, because friends like them made school unforgettable. By then we will have shared so many years that nobody will remember how it all began.

Never forget the memories, the lessons and the laughter of this special stage. Whatever happens, I hope you are happy, confident and enjoying every single moment.

With love, your senior-year self.

Sara

To herself, ten years from now

Hi, Sara!!! I’m Sara from 2026, writing this letter for you, Sara, in 2036. Right now, I’m 17 years old, and I’m finishing my last year of school. It’s a strange feeling because I’m excited about everything that’s coming, but I’m also a little scared. Tell me, did everything go well in December? Did we graduate? Was that day as emotional as I imagine? I imagine you’re studying Law at UBA. Did we actually do it? Did we ever go volunteering in Africa, like we always dreamed? And did you never stop making music? Did we finally buy the Pioneer XDJ-1000? I hope that passion never disappeared, because it has always been one of the things that makes us happiest.

Next year I am starting university, and I will probably be nervous every single day, but I know I will get through it. By 2036 I will have graduated, and I hope I will have been working long enough to feel confident in front of a judge. I am going to keep making music, so by then I will have been mixing for more than ten years.

Did you find love? Are our friends still part of your life? Are Mom and Dad healthy and happy? Most importantly: are you proud of yourself? Never forget the little pieces of the person you were in 2026. Never lose your kindness, your curiosity, your dreams, or your desire to help others. I love you so much, and I’m really proud of you, no matter where life has taken you.

See you in ten years. Sara (2026)

Ema

To herself, five years from now

Hi, I’m Ema from 2026 and I’m writing to Ema from 2031. You will be 23, and I hope that by that age you will have moved to your own place and adopted a cat. I am going to give it a silly name, I’m sure!

Are you in college? Have you started studying what I’m thinking of? I am starting university next year, so by the time you read this I will have been studying for almost five years, and I hope I will be close to finishing my degree. I hope I will be living an organized life. Maybe I will be travelling more and meeting new people, and I am going to make sure I take lots of photos of everything.

I will be working towards my dreams, and I will have learned from my mistakes and grown as a person. By then I will have made new friends, but I hope I will still have the old ones next to me, because they are the ones who make me laugh the most.

When you read this again, you will have achieved many of your goals. Please never give up and always believe in yourself.

See you in 5 years, me.

Sadisley

To herself, ten years from now

Dear future me / Hi Sadis,

It is a very long time to wait for a letter, but I hope you have become a patient person and that you are doing what you love. Today, I am thinking about studying at the vet school at UBA. I hope that in ten years you will have finished that career. Also, I know that it is not that easy, but I am sure you can do it.

I am starting that journey next year, so by 2036 I will have been working with animals for several years. Maybe you will have opened a small clinic where nobody is ever scared of the vet. I am going to be so proud of you, no matter how many exams you had to repeat!

On the other hand, I hope you will stay in contact with our friends who have been with us since we were kids. I really hope you are going to be happy with your family, living alone with your pets, and taking plenty of peaceful naps with them.

Kisses,
Sadisley (from 2026)

Anecdotes and school trips

The moments that turned into the stories we still tell each other.

The day Francisco fell into the river

School trip to Bariloche, 2022

In 2022 our whole year travelled to Bariloche on the school trip we had been looking forward to for months. We were staying near the lake, and every morning our teachers took us on a different excursion: we climbed to viewpoints, walked through the forest and learned about the nature of the region. The purpose of the trip was to enjoy the landscape and to spend time together as a group before the end of school.

One afternoon, while we were walking beside a river, everybody stopped to take photos. Francisco was standing on a wet rock when he suddenly slipped and fell straight into the water! For a second nobody moved, because we were terrified that he had hurt himself. Then he stood up, soaking wet but perfectly fine, and we burst out laughing. The poor guy was shivering, embarrassed and a little proud at the same time, and a teacher lent him a dry jacket.

It was hilarious and unforgettable, and it showed us how close we were as a group. We would repeat the trip tomorrow, although next time we would bring spare socks for everyone.

The night Sadisley flooded the cabin

School trip to Mendoza

We went on a trip to Mendoza with the school, and we were all thrilled because we had never been so close to the mountains. During the day we visited a turquoise reservoir surrounded by snowy peaks, tried the local food and took hundreds of photos in the freezing wind. At night we slept in cabins, and the four of us had chosen one together.

Everything was going perfectly until one night Sadisley decided to take her time in the shower. When we realised what was happening, the whole ground floor had flooded and everything on the floor was drenched. We were shocked at first, and then we started laughing nervously while we were cleaning up with every towel we could find. Sadis ended up cleaning the most, since she was the one who had caused the flood in the first place, and she was embarrassed but laughed along with us.

It is the kind of silly, happy memory that makes a trip special. Our teachers came with us, and the aim was to learn about the region and bond as a group. We would love to repeat it, but next time we would check the drain first.

Pascua Joven

The Easter retreat at school

Every year our school organises Pascua Joven, an Easter retreat for the older students. When we walked into the sports hall that morning, it was decorated with ribbons and a huge banner, and hundreds of students were already gathered inside. I was nervous at first because I did not know how the day was going to be, but a few minutes later we were singing, playing games and talking in small groups.

What I remember most is the atmosphere: there was so much laughter, and there were also quiet moments when everyone was thinking about friendship, gratitude and the people who had been by our side. We had never been so honest with each other, and I felt calm, grateful and a little emotional by the end of the day. Teachers and coordinators accompanied us the whole time and made sure that everybody felt welcome.

It was heartwarming, and it taught us that being together matters more than anything we do. We would gladly repeat it, although we would have liked it to last longer.

Marching in formation

A school ceremony

Our favourite people at school

Two people whose classrooms, and pep talks, we’ll remember long after the bell stops ringing.

Lula Antonucci

Primary school teacher and first-year preceptora

Lula Antonucci is the teacher who welcomed us in primary school and the preceptora who looked after us during our first year of secondary school. Thanks to her we learned about computers, which was completely new for us, and we also laughed a lot in her classes. She is cheerful, charismatic and patient, and she is always there when we need her. We will never forget the smell of incense in the preceptoría, which used to take all the bad vibes out of the room. She is the kind of person who listens before she speaks and who makes every student feel important. We are lucky to have had her, because she was part of the most important place in our lives: school.

Jimena Tello

Preceptora

Jimena Tello is a preceptora who has always helped us when we had problems. She is responsible, supportive, reliable, kind and patient, and she listens carefully to everyone who needs advice or encouragement. She also helps to organise school activities, which makes our school a better place, and she is someone whose door is always open. She makes us feel comfortable, which is not easy in a school with so many students. We admire the way she treats every student fairly and with respect, and we are grateful for her support, which we will remember for a long time.

Advice for freshmen

What we would tell the students who are just starting.

If we could give some advice to younger students, we would tell them to enjoy every moment of their school years, because time goes by faster than they think. When it comes to subjects and homework, try to stay organized, pay attention in class and don’t be scared of Felisa, she’s fine. Managing your time is important, but remember that you also need time to rest and enjoy yourself.

We would also tell them that friendship is one of the most important parts of school life. Make friends, meet new people and don’t be afraid to be yourself. However, don’t feel pressured to fit in or compare yourself.

Be open to new experiences, participate in school activities and take every opportunity to learn something new, but do not forget that challenges and mistakes are part of growing up, so learn from them instead of being too hard on yourself. Remember that you don’t have to be perfect or have the best grades all the time. The most important thing is to cherish the journey and make good memories. These years will become some of the memories you will carry with you forever.

Memories in music

Our school playlist.

Every school year has a soundtrack, and ours is full of songs that we played on the bus to school trips, sang at the top of our voices in the courtyard and listened to with headphones the night before an exam. We put them all in one playlist, because each song takes us back to a specific moment: the excitement of the first day, the nerves before a test, the long road to Bariloche and the last days in our maroon hoodies.

Some songs remind us of friends who made us laugh, and others of calm afternoons when we were studying together. When we play the playlist now, we remember exactly who we were and how much we have grown. To listen to it, open Spotify, tap Search, then the camera icon, and scan the code below.

Thanks to school for…

We would like to thank our school for being the place where we grew up, shared experiences, and learned the values that shape who we are today: the Marist values.

Being Marist means being part of a family with truly unique qualities. The kindness, support, and understanding that this school has given us are things we will carry with us throughout our lives. Being Marist means sharing, caring, and growing together.

Thanks to our school, we have discovered who we are and who we want to become. We are grateful for all the opportunities we had to spend time together outside the classroom, whether during school retreats or camps, where laughter and heartwarming hugs were always present.

We are taking away thousands of memories, friendships, conversations, and lessons that will continue to shape us in the future.

Thank you for everything.
